subsystems.name: Quantum entropy source
subsystems.role: the physical process whose outcome is genuinely unpredictable — for example vacuum-field fluctuations or the arrival time of individual photons.

subsystems.name: Detector and digitizer
subsystems.role: turns the quantum event into an electrical, then digital, signal.

subsystems.name: Conditioning and extraction
subsystems.role: removes bias and any classical predictability, squeezing genuine entropy into uniform bits.

subsystems.name: Random-number module
subsystems.role: packages the source into a usable component with a defined output rate.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: converts the random bits into keys and gets them to where they are needed.

subsystems.name: Certification and health monitoring
subsystems.role: proves the bits are random and detects drift or tampering in service.

buildSteps.title: Choose and characterise a quantum process
buildSteps.detail: Candidates include the phase or amplitude noise of a laser, photon detection times, or vacuum fluctuations measured by a shot-noise-limited detector.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the source
buildSteps.detail: The light source and optics are built as a discrete assembly or, increasingly, a photonic integrated circuit on a semiconductor chip.

buildSteps.title: Add detection and readout
buildSteps.detail: Photons are converted to electrical pulses; single-photon detectors are used where the source produces individual quanta.

buildSteps.title: Digitise the raw signal
buildSteps.detail: The analogue output is sampled and thresholded to produce a raw bit stream.

buildSteps.title: Extract true randomness
buildSteps.detail: An extractor compresses many raw bits into fewer output bits, wiping out bias and any pattern an attacker could model.

buildSteps.title: Validate the entropy
buildSteps.detail: The design is tested against standard frameworks such as NIST SP 800-90B and BSI AIS 31 to estimate min-entropy per bit.

buildSteps.title: Package and integrate
buildSteps.detail: The module is given a driver or API and fitted into servers, hardware security modules or network equipment.

buildSteps.title: Operate with live monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Continuous health tests watch for stuck or drifting sources, and the module is replaced or re-seeded if they fail.

buildSteps.title: Wire into a security protocol
buildSteps.detail: The bits become keys for encryption — and, for the strongest claims, feed a one-time pad or a post-quantum scheme rather than being treated as a lock on their own.

prerequisites.tech: Reliable random-number generation and statistical testing
prerequisites.why: quantum sources still have to be validated and de-biased like any entropy source.
raw quantum signals are biased; extraction is what makes the output usable as key material.
many quantum entropy schemes rely on counting individual photons accurately.
randomness alone does not stop a key being copied in transit; QKD is needed for eavesdropper detection.

prerequisites.tech: Information-theoretically secure encryption and key management
prerequisites.why: the 'uncrackable' claim only holds with a one-time pad and perfect key handling, which is operationally hard.

pathway.milestone: quantum random-number generators sold as chips and rack modules for key generation
pathway.unlocks: better keys than software pseudo-random generators, especially for long-lived secrets.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale integration into processors, phones and network gear
pathway.unlocks: quantum entropy everywhere, at little cost.

pathway.milestone: combined quantum random-number and quantum key distribution links
pathway.unlocks: key exchange that detects interception, closing the copying gap.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems pairing quantum key distribution with post-quantum algorithms
pathway.unlocks: practical high assurance without relying on any single physical assumption.
